Notable changes in ODSDropdownSelect

ODSDropdownSelect has some notable changes from previous version.

items Property

Old: Required and typed as Omit<ODSDropdownSelectMenuItemProps, "selected">[].
New: Optional (items?: ODSMenuListItemProps[];) and uses the shared ODSMenuListItemProps type from @/components.
labelText Property

New: Adds a deprecated labelText property (labelText?: string;) for backward compatibility.
Note: Prefer using the new label property.
onValueChange Callback

Old: The callback parameter was { id?: string; value?: string; labelText?: string; }.
New: The callback parameter is { id?: string; value?: string; label?: string; } (renamed labelText to label).
expanded Property

New: Adds an optional expanded?: boolean; property to control the default expanded state of the dropdown.
General Improvements

The new version is more flexible, supports both controlled and uncontrolled usage, and aligns with other ODS menu/list patterns.
Migration tips:

Use the label property instead of labelText.
Pass items as ODSMenuListItemProps[].
Update your onValueChange handler to use the new callback signature.

type ODSMenuListItemSize = "large" | "small";

export type ODSMenuListItemProps = Omit<
  ODSComponentPropsWithRef<"div" | "a">,
  "onSelect" | "size"
> & {
  className?: string;
  disabled?: boolean;
  /** For an icon prefix. */
  iconBefore?: ReactNode;
  /** For an icon suffix. */
  iconAfter?: ReactNode;
  /**The variant of the item */
  variant?: "standard" | "checked" | "cascade" | "buttons";
  selected?: boolean;
  /** Callback function for when the plus icon button of the buttons variant is clicked */
  onPlusClick?: () => void;
  /** Callback function for when the minus icon button of the buttons variant is clicked */
  onMinusClick?: () => void;
  onFocus?: () => void;
  label?: string;
  /** Text for the helperText component inside the item  */
  helperText?: string;
  innerAriaLabel?: string;
  id?: string;

  onClick?: () => void;
  /** Fires when the item is selected, namely clicked.
   * Calling `event.preventDefault()` will prevent the menu from closing. */
  onSelect?: (
    event: SyntheticEvent<HTMLDivElement, Event>,
    item?: ODSMenuListItemProps
  ) => void;
  /** the size of the menu list item. will be inherited from the parent container element,
   * and will bestow it to its cascade menu, if it has one */
  size?: ODSMenuListItemSize;
  /** An alternative text for typeahead. */
  textValue?: string;
  /** props for the cascade menu of this item */
  cascadeMenuProps?: Omit<ODSMenuListContextType, "size">;
  /** href to have item act as anchor element */
  href?: string;
  /** This adds the active styling for hovered combobox list elements. */
  active?: boolean;
  /** this api is used to control the selected value of the dropdown in a controlled manner.
   * When using dropdown select as uncontrolled manner, please use `defaultValue` api
   */
  value?: string;
  /** Icon when variant is set to 'checked' */
  checkmarkIcon?: React.ReactNode;
  /** Icon when variant is set to 'cascade' */
  navigationRightIcon?: React.ReactNode;
  /** First button Icon to be displayed when variant is set to 'buttons' */
  buttonIconFirstIcon?: React.ReactNode;
  /** Second button Icon to be displayed when variant is set to 'buttons' */
  buttonIconSecondIcon?: React.ReactNode;
};

General

With a dropdown, users select a single option from a collapsible list of available options.

When to use

Use dropdowns to present selectable options in a form or to filter or sort content.

To select options within a form
To select a single option
To filter or sort content
When not to use

Few options: Use radio buttons instead of a dropdown to avoid hiding content from the user

Many choices: An input field with auto-fill is more efficient and time-saving

Several options: Use checkboxes instead of a dropdown
Anatomy


1. Label

The label clearly indicates what kind of options the dropdown provides.

2. Arrow icon

The direction of the arrow indicates whether the dropdown menu is open or closed.

3. Information (optional)

Additional information can help clarify the content or purpose of a dropdown.

4. Label and value

When a Value from the dropdown is selected, it takes the place of the Label and the Label collapses into a smaller size.

5. Expanded menu

The dropdown menu contains the available options or groups of options.

Use Directives

How designers should use the component

Support information

Selected


Dropdown contexts

If additional user feedback is needed we can show the message component.


Modes


Labels should be scannable

Make sure the user can quickly scan the labels of the menu.




Dos and dont´s


Don’t add icons to the right on the dropdown menu

The space on the right is reserved to mark which option has been selected.




Icons on the left

Either none of the options in the dropdown menu should have left icons, or all options should have icons.




Behaviours

Interactions

Expand when clicked, close when the user selects an option.


Overflow content

Avoid having multiple lines of text in a dropdown.

If the text is too long for one line, add an ellipsis (…) for overflow content, and accompany with a browser-based tooltip to show the full string of text.

Ideally, designers should avoid having options that are long enough to need truncation.


Component Variants

Standard


Informative


Error


Colour Schemes

How it works (or is restricted) across colour schemes

White


Black


Magenta

This component can only be used on neutral colour schemes


Secondary

This component can only be used on neutral colour schemes


Accessibility

This OneDS component is compliant with WCAG 2.2 AA Standards.

Key considerations for keyboard interactions and screen readers are included. Additionally, all components meet requirements for the contrast ratios.

Design considerations

Provide clear and short option label.
A disabled dropdown select must not have a support message, and its label should not convey any crucial information needed to understand the context.
Refer to the AX annotation guide for detailed designer instructions on accessibility annotations.

Development considerations

No further development considerations required.

While this individual component is accessible, building fully usable interfaces requires further attention. For guidance, refer to our OneExperience accessibility resources.
